info.title: Forma runtime API: the ai-sdk-v5 client
info.description:
A Forma runtime serves one agent (or, multi-tenant, every deployed agent) to one kind of client, which its runtime file names (`client:`). The paths are the same for every client; what they take and return is not. This describes one client.

**`client: ai-sdk-v5`**: the protocol of [Vercel's AI SDK](https://ai-sdk.dev/) (v5), for front-ends built with it. The SDK sends only the last message, and Forma keeps the conversation.

Requests come from your back-end, which authenticates the user and says who they are (`X-User-ID`): Forma checks the API key, not the user.

post.summary:
Sends a message, and streams what the agent does, in the AI SDK's
protocol.
post.description:
Meant for the AI SDK's `useChat`, with a transport that sends only the
last message (Forma keeps the conversation; the SDK's default is to
send all of it). The message is a `UIMessage`: an `id`, a `role`
(`user`), and its `parts`. The answer is the SDK's UI message stream:
`start`, text and reasoning parts, tool calls, files, Forma's own
`data-*` parts, `finish`, and a last line with what the job consumed.

A call that needs an answer is announced as a `tool-input-available`
that gets no output: answer it with `/v1/resume`. How the
conversation goes on otherwise is as with the `sync` client.

parameters.name: X-User-ID
parameters.description:
The user who writes. Forma does not check it: your back-end
authenticates the user, and sends their id. It must be the user who
started the conversation.

parameters.name: X-Session-ID
parameters.description:
The conversation, as `/v1/init` returned it. Required when the server
keeps conversations (any `storage` but `none`); otherwise every
message is a conversation of its own.

parameters.name: X-User-Roles
parameters.description:
The user's roles, comma-separated (`admin, editor`): which tools the
agent may call for them (a tool's `just_for`). Not checked either:
your back-end sends what it knows.

parameters.name: X-Time-Zone
parameters.description:
The user's time zone, as an IANA name (`America/Santiago`): what the
`current-date` tool answers in, before the agent's own `timezone`. A
name that is not a time zone is ignored.

parameters.name: X-Deployment-ID
parameters.description:
Multi-tenant servers only: which deployment (agent) to talk to, as the
manager returned it when deploying it. Set by your reverse proxy, from
what it authenticated: never from what the client sent.

requestBody.description: The user's message, as the AI SDK sends it: `role` must be `user`, and `parts` cannot be empty. Attachments travel inline, and the body can be 2 MB at most.

200.description: A stream of Server-Sent Events: the AI SDK's UI message stream. Each `data:` line holds one JSON object: an event (with a `type`), or, last, the job's usage (without one).

400.description: The body is not a user message with parts (a JSON `{"error": ...}`), or a header is missing (plain text)

403.description: The `X-API-Key` is wrong, or the conversation belongs to another user

404.description: There is no such conversation (or, multi-tenant, deployment)

409.description: The agent is still answering the conversation's previous message: wait, and send it again

413.description: The body is larger than 2 MB (attachments included)

500.description: The server has no `FORMA_AGENT_KEY`, or its storage failed

get.description:
Creates a conversation for the user, and returns its id: send it as
`X-Session-ID` with every message of it. A conversation never ends:
start a new one whenever the user wants a fresh start. In a server
that keeps no conversations (`storage: none`), it returns a
placeholder, and stores nothing.

parameters.name: X-User-ID
parameters.description:
The user the conversation is for. Forma does not check it: your
back-end authenticates the user, and sends their id. Only the user who
started a conversation can write in it. Required when the server keeps
conversations (any `storage` but `none`).

parameters.name: X-Deployment-ID
parameters.description:
Multi-tenant servers only: which deployment (agent) to talk to, as the
manager returned it when deploying it. Set by your reverse proxy, from
what it authenticated: never from what the client sent.

400.description: A header is missing (`X-User-ID`; `X-Deployment-ID` in a multi-tenant server)

404.description: Multi-tenant servers: there is no such deployment

500.description: The server has no `FORMA_AGENT_KEY`, or its storage failed

post.summary:
Answers the tool call a conversation waits on, and waits for the
agent's answer.
post.description:
The request is as with the `sync` client, and so is the answer (one
JSON object, not a stream), but its message is in the AI SDK's shape.
It does not stream because the AI SDK's handling of human in the loop
does not work with a resumed stream.

200.description: The agent answered (`completed`), stopped at another call (`suspended`), or waits for the turn's other calls (`still_suspended`)

400.description: The call is not waiting for an answer (it does not exist, was answered, or a new message rejected it); the body is not valid JSON, or has both or neither of `arguments` and `result`; a header is missing; or the server keeps no conversations

403.description: The `X-API-Key` is wrong, or the conversation belongs to another user

404.description: There is no such conversation (or, multi-tenant, deployment)

409.description: The agent is still working on the conversation

422.description: The body is not a resume request

oneOf.description: The stream was aborted.
The agent failed; the stream ends here.
The agent started working on the message. Always the first event.

messageId.description: The id of the job, which the usage report at the end repeats.

oneOf.description: A text part begins.

id.description: The id shared by the part's `text-delta`s and `text-end`.

oneOf.description: More text for the part `id` began.

delta.description: The text, to append to what came before.

id.description: The part this text belongs to.

oneOf.description: The text part `id` is complete.
A reasoning part begins (models that expose their reasoning).

id.description: The id shared by the part's deltas and end.

oneOf.description: More reasoning for the part `id`.

delta.description: The reasoning, to append to what came before.

id.description: The part this reasoning belongs to.

oneOf.description: The reasoning part `id` is complete.
The agent is about to call a tool.

toolCallId.description: The call's id, which its input and output repeat.

toolName.description: The tool's name, as the agent defines it.

oneOf.description:
The arguments of a tool call. Also how a call that waits for an answer
(an approval, or a delegated tool's result) is announced: the stream
then ends without its output, and the call is answered with
`/v1/resume`.

input.description: The arguments, as the model wrote them.

oneOf.description: What a tool call returned.
The job is done, and its turn stored: the next message can be sent.

A file produced during the turn: an image a tool generated, a file it
fetched, or media the model returned. The AI SDK's own file part.

url.description: A `data:` URL, or a URL the client can reach.

oneOf.description:
Answer to a `/v1/resume`: other calls of the same turn are still
waiting for an answer.
How well the answer is grounded in the sources it used.
A document used as a source for the answer.

AiSdkV5Event.description:
One event of the stream the `ai-sdk-v5` client sends, in the protocol of
Vercel's AI SDK (v5): each is the JSON of one `data:` line.

`type` says what happened. Text, reasoning and tool calls follow the AI
SDK's own UI message stream parts; what only Forma reports travels as the
SDK's custom `data-*` parts.

AiSdkV5FilePart.description: The AI SDK's file part: a picture or a document, by URL.

url.description:
A `data:` URL; or, for a picture, a URL the model's provider can
reach. Other files must be inline: Forma does not fetch them.

oneOf.description: Something that happened.

What the job consumed. The last line of a stream that was not cut
short by an error.

AiSdkV5Line.description:
One `data:` line of the `ai-sdk-v5` client's stream: an event of the AI
SDK's UI message stream, and, last, what the job consumed.

AiSdkV5Message.description:
A message, as Vercel's AI SDK (v5) sends it (a `UIMessage`): an id, who
wrote it, and its parts.

id.description: The message's id. Required, and not kept.

parts.description:
What it says: the AI SDK's `text` and `file` parts, or OpenAI's
(`image_url`, `input_audio`, `file`).

role.description: Who wrote it: `user`, for what is sent to the agent.

oneOf.description:
The AI SDK's own file part, which is how `useChat` sends attachments,
and how Forma sends files back.

One of OpenAI's parts. The AI SDK's `text` part is the same as
OpenAI's.

AiSdkV5Part.description: One part of an AI SDK message.

UsageTally.description:
Groups [`SSEvent::Usage`] events by `(provider, server_address, model)`, lists the kind of
every tool called ([`SSEvent::ToolInputAvailable`]), and sums
[`SSEvent::ToolUsage`] by kind and unit.

tokens.description:
What each provider and model consumed, one entry per pair.

Insertion-ordered so a run's first model leads the report, which makes
logs and fixtures stable to read.

tool_usage.description: What tools consumed in units of their own (absent when nothing).

tools.description: The kind of every tool called, once per call.

AudioFormat.description: Specifies the output audio format. Must be one of wav, mp3, flac, opus, or pcm16.

EmptyData.description: The `data` of an event that carries nothing.

FileTag.description: The tag of the AI SDK's file part.

score.description: How well the answer is supported by its sources.

MessageRejection.description:
A request Forma refused before reading it as a message: its body is not
JSON, is not a message, has no content, or is not the user's.

calls.description: Provider round trips, which some plans bill per-request on top of tokens.

model.description: The model the provider reports having served.

provider.description:
The backend that served the calls, by its OpenTelemetry GenAI name
(`ollama`, `openai`, `groq`, `gcp.vertex_ai`).

server_address.description:
The host the calls went to (OpenTelemetry's `server.address`): with
`provider`, who served them, and so who bills them. Every
OpenAI-compatible server speaks `openai`; the host tells them apart.

ModelUsage.description:
What one `(provider, server_address, model)` consumed across a whole run.

Provider is half the key, not decoration: the same model name reached
through two backends is two different prices, and through a local Ollama it
is free.

session_id.description:
The conversation's id: send it as `X-Session-ID` with every message
of it. A server that keeps no conversations (`storage: none`) returns
a placeholder, which it ignores.

OpenAIFile.description: A file: a document, or audio in any container.

file_data.description: The base64 encoded file data, used when passing the file to the model as a string.

file_id.description: The ID of an uploaded file to use as input.

filename.description: The name of the file, used when passing the file to the model as a string.

oneOf.description: How closely the model should look at it.

url.description:
A `data:` URL (`data:image/png;base64,...`), or a URL the model's
provider can reach.

format.description: The format of the encoded audio data. Currently supports "wav" and "mp3".

oneOf.description: Text.
An image.

allOf.description: A recording, base64 with its format named.

oneOf.description: A recording, base64 with its format named.

allOf.description: A file, base64 in a `data:` URL.

oneOf.description: A file, base64 in a `data:` URL.

OpenAIMessagePart.description: One piece of a message's content, its `type` saying what it is.

OpenAIVisionDetail.description: Tells the model what level of detail to use when processing and understanding the image

extractiveAnswer.description: Passages that answer the question directly, if the source gave any.

snippet.description: The passage that was used, if known.

ResumeRequest.description: The request body for the resume endpoints.

arguments.description: Arguments to pass to the tool (required when `reject` is false).

reject.description:
If `true`, the call is rejected: the tool does not run, and the model
is told the user rejected it.

result.description: The result of the tool call (required when `reject` is false).

tool_call_id.description: ID of the pending tool call this feedback applies to.

TokenUsage.description:
What one LLM call consumed, in the shape a bill needs.

This is a *normalisation* of [`OpenAIUsage`], not a copy of it. Providers
disagree about what their totals include, and the disagreement shows up as
a wrong invoice rather than a parse error, so the convention is pinned here,
once, at the only layer that still knows which provider produced the numbers:

- `input_tokens` counts every prompt token, `cached_input_tokens` included.
- `output_tokens` counts every generated token, `reasoning_tokens` included.

`cached_input_tokens` and `reasoning_tokens` are therefore *subsets* of their
parents, carried separately because they are priced differently — cached
input is discounted, reasoning is billed at the output rate. Adding either to
its parent double-charges.

cached_input_tokens.description:
The subset of `input_tokens` the provider served from its prompt cache.
Billed at a discount, so ignoring it over-charges.

input_audio_tokens.description:
Audio tokens in the prompt, a subset of `input_tokens`. Priced far above
text tokens by every provider that supports them.

output_audio_tokens.description: Audio tokens generated, a subset of `output_tokens`.

reasoning_tokens.description:
The subset of `output_tokens` spent on reasoning the client never sees.
Billed like any other output token.

ToolUsage.description:
What a tool consumed beyond being called, in a unit it is priced by: the
seconds a code-execution sandbox ran, for instance. Summed per
`(tool_kind, unit)` across a run.

quantity.description: How many `unit`s, over the whole job.

oneOf.description:
Every call was answered, and the agent answered: `data` is its
message.

data.description:
A message, as Vercel's AI SDK (v5) sends it (a `UIMessage`): an id, who
wrote it, and its parts.

id.description: The message's id. Required, and not kept.

parts.description:
What it says: the AI SDK's `text` and `file` parts, or OpenAI's
(`image_url`, `input_audio`, `file`).

role.description: Who wrote it: `user`, for what is sent to the agent.

oneOf.description: The agent went on, and stopped at another call that needs an answer.

data.description: The agent went on, and stopped at another call that needs an answer.

tool_call_id.description:
The id of the call waiting for an answer: what `/v1/resume`
answers.

tool_name.description: The tool the agent wants to call.

oneOf.description:
Other calls of the same turn are still waiting for an answer: the
agent goes on once all are answered.

allOf.description:
Result from a Resume, indicating whether the
request was completed, whether the resumed run stopped at a new call
that needs an answer, or whether the session is still
suspended (other calls are waiting for an answer).

A rejected call is completed like any other: the rejection becomes the
call's result, and the agent answers with it.

usage.description:
What the job consumed: tokens per provider and model, and the tools
it called. Empty when nothing ran (`still_suspended`).

ResumeAnswer.description: A JSON answer: its `status` and `data`, and what producing it consumed.

api_key.name: X-API-Key
api_key.description: The server's `FORMA_AGENT_KEY`. Not required when the runtime file says `no_api_key: true`. It identifies your back-end, not the user: keep it out of browsers and apps, and put a back-end of your own in front of the agent.

tags.name: Conversations
tags.description: Start a conversation, write in it, and answer the tool calls it waits on.
